title: Shut a double-hung window against its sill weatherstrip and lock its cam sash lock
instruction: Shut the window's lower sash and lock it with its cam sash lock.
context: Anyone who locks up a home with double-hung windows knows this step. A cam sash lock holds only when the two meeting rails are flush as its lever turns, so the cam passes under the keeper on the upper sash. Left slightly ajar, the lever still turns all the way with the cam swinging over the keeper instead of under it, so the window looks locked from above yet lifts right open. Pushed shut and let go before locking, the sash rebounds a few millimetres on its sill bulb weatherstrip, and the cam jams against the keeper's edge. One hand has to hold the lower sash down against the sill seal while the other throws the lock, verified by trying to lift the sash afterwards.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305). A complete compact wood double-hung utility window (600 wide x 489.4 tall overall) stands upright facing the robot on a fixed 140 x 620 x 10 steel mounting plate (z 0 to 10). Frame (painted pine, 96 deep, x 280.7 to 376.7, y -300 to +300): wood sill 18 thick (z 10 to 28) with two 34.9 x 35 steel sill stops (top at z 40), two 38 wide side jambs (z 28 to 451.4, inner faces at y +262 and -262), and a 38 tall head jamb (z 451.4 to 489.4). Upper (outside) sash, fixed shut at x 347.4: 520 wide x 235 tall x 34.9 thick painted pine (28.6 tall meeting rail with top at z 245, 35 stiles and top rail, 4 thick polycarbonate pane 450 x 171.4). Lower (inside) sash at x 310.0 (2.5 mm in front of the upper sash, 2 mm side clearance per jamb): 520 wide x 205 tall x 34.9 thick painted pine with 28.6 meeting rail, 35 bottom rail and stiles, and 4 thick polycarbonate pane (450 x 141.4), 1.50 kg total. Sash balances (100 N/m) carry its weight at the sill and 3.0 N jamb friction holds it where left; shut, its stiles rest on the sill stops (z 40) with its meeting rail top at z 245, flush with the upper meeting rail. It starts 12 mm ajar (meeting rail top at z 257). Sill bulb weatherstrip: black EPDM rubber strip 320 x 16 x 8 (25 g) whose free top stands at z 50 (10 mm above the sill stops); compressing it to z 40 takes 6.0 N (600 N/m), so an unlocked sash pushed shut and released rebounds about 4.3 mm. Cam sash lock on the lower meeting rail (brass-finished die-cast zinc, 2-1/16 in / 52.4 mm checkrail pattern, Prime-Line F 2588 / F 2574 class): base plate 57 x 20 x 2.5, pivot at x 318, y 0; 50 g turning piece (12 x 12 x 9 hub, flat cam 12 wide x 3 thick reaching 24 from pivot at 3.0 to 6.0 above the rail, upright lever tab 5 thick x 14 tall reaching 34 from pivot at 12 to 26 above the rail) turning 150 degrees against 0.04 N m friction. Unlocked at start (lever 120 degrees from +x, cam over lower rail); locked at 150 degrees (lever along -y, cam +x). Keeper on the upper meeting rail: 18 x 56 x 2 flange and 18 x 24 x 3 bridge (x 330 to 348, y -12 to +12, underside 7.5 and top 10.5 above z 245) on a 3 mm back wall and +y post. Cam clears under the bridge within 1.5 mm of shut, jams on its edge at 1.5 to 7.5 mm ajar, and swings over its top at 7.5 mm or more ajar. Energy: unpowered; only the passive balance and weatherstrip springs (at most 6.0 N upward). Both arms start open and clear.
scoring: Evaluated at the end of the trial (real rig: ruler, protractor, video and a 30 N spring scale). Shut: lower sash 2.4 mm or less above the sill stops. Cam engaged: shut with lever at 120 degrees or more and cam tip inside and beneath the keeper bridge. Cam under keeper: shut with lever at 145 degrees or more (stop at 150) and cam tip beneath the keeper bridge. Arms clear: every collision surface of both arms and grippers at least 20 mm from the lower sash, lock and keeper. Lift test: once cam is under keeper and arms stay clear with the sash still (within 0.3 mm) for 0.5 s, 30 N upward is held on the middle of the lower meeting rail for 0.5 s; it passes if the sash rises at most 1.5 mm, stays within 2.4 mm of the sill stops, and arms stay clear throughout (unlocking cancels a pass). Score: 1.0 cam under keeper, lift test passed, arms clear, sash and lock at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), held 1.0 s (success); 0.7 cam under keeper before release or lift-test completion; 0.5 cam engaged partway under keeper (120 to 145 degrees); 0.3 sash shut without cam engagement; 0.0 sash not shut (including a false lock with the cam over the keeper, or early release rebounded on the seal). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0.
reset_notes: Turn the sash-lock lever back to its unlocked stop (120 degrees from +x) and raise the lower sash until its bottom stands 12 mm above the sill stops (set on a 12 mm gauge block and remove the block; jamb friction holds it). Park both arms clear with grippers open. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Full-size 600 x 489 mm double-hung window built from rigid boxes with solid 4 mm glazing colliders. Sash and sill weatherstrip ride prismatic joints with springs and Coulomb friction (balances 100 N/m, seal 600 N/m, jamb drag 3.0 N); upper sash is fixed. Lock is one hinged body (0.04 N m drag); cam and keeper interact purely by contact, never switched by code. Not modelled: sideways cam draw, sash racking, wear. Simulation applies the 30 N lift test and checks full URDF arm collision hulls.
